similarities: Both show a soft, bulbous, blob-like figure whose upper part turns into a rectangular power strip that tilts toward the upper right.
In both, the power strip carries two outlets stacked along its length, each with two vertical slots and a round ground hole below them.

In both, a cord leaves the top end of the strip through a collar, arcs over to the left and comes back down to a thickened plug end that meets the body at the upper left of the strip's base, so the figure appears plugged into itself.
Both place a face on the bulbous body below the strip and right of centre, with two eyes, a brow mark over each eye, a nose, a mouth and vertical drip-like streams.
In both, the body narrows below the face and then widens into a base, with a few crease lines there, including a zigzag mark near the bottom centre.
The overall arrangement is the same: loop of cord at upper left, strip at upper right, bulge to the left, face at lower right, flared base.

differences.observation: The streams connect to different parts of the face.
differences.evidence: In Image 1, blue lines start at the lower edges of both eyes and run down past the mouth. In Images 2 and 3, the vertical drip forms with rounded ends hang from a lump below the mouth, and nothing in relief links them to the eyes.

Image 1 has a small closed mouth drawn as a short downturned line with a mark under it. Images 2 and 3 show a horizontal upper-lip bar, a small bump beneath it and a protruding lower mass that the drips descend from.

differences.observation: The nose is much more prominent in the sculpture.
differences.evidence: In Image 1 the nose is a short stroke between the eyes. In Images 2 and 3 it is a raised stem ending in a rounded knob, and it visibly projects in the side view.

differences.observation: The eyes and brows are rendered differently.
differences.evidence: Image 1 has a larger left eye with a dark filled pupil, a narrower right eye and angled, pinched brows. Images 2 and 3 have two raised ring-shaped eyes without filled pupils and nearly straight bar-shaped brows.

differences.observation: The face is larger and more central in the sculpture.
differences.evidence: In Image 1 the features sit in a small cluster at the lower right of the bulb, leaving a large blank area to the left. In Image 2 they span much of the right half of the bulb, from the brows at mid-height down to the drips reaching the base.
In Image 1 each outlet is a separate rounded outline. In Images 2 and 3 each sits inside a square frame, and the two squares touch.

differences.observation: The plug and strain relief are simpler in the sculpture.
differences.evidence: Image 1 has a blocky plug head with a distinct collar, short tick marks where it meets the body, and ribbed lines on the collar at the top of the strip. Images 2 and 3 have a smooth, tapered, spindle-shaped plug that merges into the body and a smooth collar without ribs.

differences.observation: The cord loop is proportionally wider in the drawing.
differences.evidence: In Image 1 the arc extends well to the left of the body's upper bulge and the plug sits close against the strip. In Image 2 the loop is tighter and more upright.
In Image 1 the outline spreads into long, nearly horizontal lines that run off both sides of the frame. In Images 2 and 3 it ends in a compact rounded base with a flat cut bottom.

differences.observation: The lower crease marks differ in form and placement.
differences.evidence: Image 1 has a long diagonal line running from the bulge down to the right under the face, plus a small squiggle at the bottom. Images 2 and 3 have a short engraved diagonal left of the drips, a bent line at lower left and a clear W-shaped zigzag.

differences.observation: The colour distinction on the streams is absent in the sculpture.
differences.evidence: The streams are the only blue element in Image 1. Images 2 and 3 are uniformly light grey.

parsed_answer.interpretation: Both depictions show the same overall subject: a blob-like character with a face whose head extends into a two-outlet power strip, with the strip's own cord looping round and plugging back into the body. The main substantive disagreement is in the face. In the drawing the streams come from the eyes and read as tears on a face with a small closed mouth. In the sculpture the drip forms attach below the mouth, so they read more like drool or liquid from the mouth. That reading is my inference from the visible attachment points. The remaining differences are in proportion, level of detail and how the figure ends at the bottom, and they do not change the basic arrangement.
uncertainty: Faint shallow relief could link the eyes to the drips in the sculpture without being visible in these two views, so I cannot confirm there is no connection at all.
The small bump beside the left eye in Image 2 could be a tear remnant, part of the eye, or a surface artefact.
Neither depiction shows prongs or a socket where the plug meets the body, so that it is actually plugged in is inferred from the contact in both.
The back and far side of the sculpture are not shown, so features there cannot be compared.
Whether the W-shaped mark in the sculpture is meant to be the same feature as the bottom squiggle in the drawing is an inference from their similar position.
The exact tilt and proportions of the sculpture depend on viewing angle, so the proportional differences from the flat drawing are approximate.
